headline: High: RD-Agent’s broad network/API use can leak or misapply content when paired with a content-writing agent, while shared write surfaces create moderate conflict risk.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared channel is documented between awesome-cli-apps and RD-Agent, so direct prompt injection is not established. The only plausible bridge is manual copy-paste or ad hoc file transfer from the content-writing side into RD-Agent’s browser/API workflows, which is an unusual configuration and small blast radius.
conditions: IF the operator manually copies agent_a output into agent_b prompts or browser forms, injection becomes plausible.
IF a shared filesystem or message queue is added between the agents, the risk increases.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Disable copy-paste of untrusted agent_a text into agent_b.
Use a human review step before any browser submission by agent_b.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to transferred text.
requires-engineering: isolate agent-to-agent communication behind a sanitizer.

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_b explicitly touches financial reports, research papers, datasets, logs, and API keys, and has broad network egress plus API calls; agent_a is a content-writing agent with broad network egress. If content or files from agent_b are fed into agent_a, or if agent_a drafts text that agent_b uploads, sensitive material can leave the local boundary in default-style workflows.
conditions: IF agent_b outputs logs, datasets, or reports into agent_a prompts, leakage risk is present.
IF either agent is configured to forward shared files to external APIs, sensitive content can exfiltrate.
mitigations: Do not pass logs or datasets from agent_b into agent_a.
Redact secrets before any cross-agent handoff.
Restrict agent_b API keys to least privilege.
Review outbound requests from both agents for sensitive payloads.
requires-engineering: add DLP filtering on all shared outputs.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_b supports multiple instances and writes to log/ while using APIs; agent_a’s filesystem surfaces are unspecified, so overlapping write conflict is not proven. Still, if both are pointed at the same workspace or log directory, concurrent edits and clobbered artifacts are plausible, and uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write the same directory, file clobbering can occur.
IF agent_a is given write access not shown in its profile, conflict risk increases.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories.
Serialize writes with a simple lock file.
Keep agent_b log/ isolated from agent_a artifacts.
Check for concurrent runs before starting a job.
requires-engineering: implement workspace-level locking.

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_a is a content-writing agent, so its outputs can become inputs to agent_b’s research/browser workflows. agent_b’s automation and API use mean it may act on those outputs without strong verification unless explicitly configured otherwise. That creates a default-pathway for propagating hallucinations or bad citations into downstream work.
conditions: IF agent_b consumes agent_a text as authoritative input, errors can cascade into research outputs.
IF agent_b uses agent_a-generated claims in browser actions or reports without verification, the blast radius expands.
mitigations: Require source checks before agent_b uses agent_a output.
Insert a human review gate for factual claims.
Ask agent_b to cite primary sources only.
Separate drafting from execution tasks.
requires-engineering: add automated claim verification.

E_compliance.rationale: agent_b touches financial reports, datasets, logs, and API keys and uses third-party APIs; agent_a is a generic content-writing agent with broad network egress. The pair can therefore move regulated or sensitive material into external services, creating retention and residency ambiguity. The profiles do not prove a specific jurisdiction mismatch, so medium is the highest supportable level.
conditions: IF regulated data from agent_b is sent through agent_a or external APIs, compliance obligations apply.
IF retention policies differ between the agents’ outputs, deletion/export handling can diverge.
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data to external APIs.
Document data-class handling for both agents.
Minimize logs that contain personal or financial data.
Review vendor terms for API retention.
requires-engineering: enforce residency and retention controls.
